text: A golden record is the single, trusted, best-available version of a master data entity — the one answer everything else gets measured against.

It's not just picking your most trusted system's record and ignoring the rest — that's privileging one incomplete source over others. It's not a copy of any single original. And it's not static — it updates as source systems change.

Once matching has found the records that refer to the same entity, building the golden record means deciding, attribute by attribute, which source's value is most trustworthy. Phone from the CRM, billing address from the ERP, email from whichever system confirmed it most recently.

The result is often more complete than any single source. Phone: sourced from the CRM. Address: sourced from the ERP. Email: sourced from whichever system is freshest. One merged row, built from three partial ones.
Next: survivorship rules — the explicit, documented logic that decides which source wins for each attribute, instead of leaving it to guesswork.
